questions.question_text: 5,6-methylenedioxyindole is treated with oxalyl chloride to give a keto acid chloride. The method is useful for introducing a two carbon side chain at
questions.explanation: Electrophilic substitution of indole with oxalyl chloride typically occurs at the most electron-rich 3-position.

questions.question_text: Identify X in the following reaction involving a guanidine derivative and an alkylating or amine component: CH3-C(NH.HCl)(CH3)3 + X -> product structure containing a pyrimidine/triazine-like core.

options.A: Structure with central ring containing NH, C=N, and terminal NH2
options.B: Structure containing an allene/alkene side chain with N-H3C
options.C: Structure with N-CH3 and cyclic amidine system
options.D: Structure with terminal NH2 and simple ring

questions.explanation: Reaction of amidines/guanidines with appropriate bifunctional reagents yields substituted heterocyclic ring systems.

questions.question_text: An antineoplastic agent methotrexate inhibits the enzyme dihydrofolatereductase. They bind so tightly that their inhibition has been termed "pseudo irreversible"- basis of the binding is due to:
questions.explanation: The tight binding of methotrexate to DHFR is largely attributed to the 2,4-diaminopyrimidine ring which forms strong hydrogen bonds with the active site.

questions.question_text: $\beta$-lactamase inhibitor clavulanic acid is

options.D: 1-oxopenem structure and has no 6-acyl amino side chain of Penicillin

questions.explanation: Clavulanic acid contains an oxazolidine ring fused with a $\beta$-lactam ring (oxapenam nucleus) lacking the traditional 6-acylamino side chain.

questions.question_text: A mixture of following gases can be used in flame photometry to get a temperature of $2045^\circ\text{C}$
questions.explanation: The hydrogen-air flame provides a lower temperature, around $2000-2045^\circ\text{C}$, suitable for easily excitable alkali metals.

questions.question_text: Tesla is a unit to express:
questions.explanation: Tesla (T) is the SI derived unit of magnetic field induction (magnetic field strength).

questions.question_text: A monochromator is not used in
questions.explanation: Fourier Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectrometers use an interferometer instead of a traditional dispersive monochromator.

questions.question_text: The properties of solutions containing surface active agents change sharply over a narrow concentration range is called as
questions.explanation: Critical micellar concentration (CMC) is the concentration of surfactants above which micelles form and physical properties abruptly change.

questions.question_text: Certain suspensions with a high percentage of dispersed solids exhibit a resistance to flow with increasing rates of shear. Such systems actually increase in volume when sheared and are termed as:
questions.explanation: Dilatant systems exhibit shear-thickening behavior and an increase in volume (dilatancy) upon high rates of shear.

questions.question_text: In the process of sugar coating of tablets the colorants are added in one of the following steps:
questions.explanation: Colorants are typically added during the syrup coating or coloring stage of sugar coating.

questions.question_text: Metered dose inhalers documentation records shall show one of the information in addition to the GMP:

options.B: Records of rejection during on line check weighing

questions.explanation: In-process quality control records such as rejection logs during on-line check weighing are mandatory for MDIs.

questions.question_text: A drug which inhibits mycobacterial RNA polymerase and is very useful in treating Mycobacterium avium complex is:
questions.explanation: Rifabutin is a rifamycin derivative that inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase and is effective against Mycobacterium avium complex.

questions.question_text: A 80 years old lady suffering from osteoarthritis of hip and knee joints is given diclofenac 50 mg thrice daily and paracetamol 1 gm asrequire. She complains of passing black stools. This symptom is due to

options.C: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding due to diclofenac
options.D: Age related decrease in gastrointestinal motility

questions.explanation: Melena (black stools) in a patient taking NSAIDs like diclofenac is a classic sign of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

questions.question_text: Terazosin, an antihypertensive drug acts by:
questions.explanation: Terazosin is a selective $\alpha_1$-adrenergic blocker used to treat hypertension and BPH.

questions.question_text: An imidazole aromatase inhibitor which is effective in reducing estrogen level is
questions.explanation: Anastrozole is a non-steroidal, triazole/imidazole-class aromatase inhibitor.

questions.question_text: The main constituent in the dried ripe seeds of Colchicum luteum and Colchicum autumnale Linn. is derived from
questions.explanation: Colchicine is an alkaloid whose biosynthesis is derived from phenylalanine and tyrosine precursors.

questions.question_text: Formation of somatic embryos or embryogenic tissue directly from the explant without the formation of an intermediate callus phase is
questions.explanation: Direct somatic embryogenesis occurs when embryos develop directly from explant cells without a callus intermediary.

questions.question_text: While performing chemomicroscopy of a drug lignified trichomes were observe. Probable drug is
questions.explanation: Nux vomica seed coat powders characteristically feature lignified trichomes.

questions.question_text: A common organism that causes meningitis belongs to the genus
questions.explanation: Neisseria meningitidis is a leading bacterial cause of meningitis.

questions.question_text: Bradykinin is
questions.explanation: Bradykinin is a physiologically active peptide composed of nine amino acids (nonapeptide).

questions.question_text: Identify the correct combination of the intermediate X and the product Y in the given Grignard reaction scheme.
questions.explanation: Standard Grignard addition to an ester followed by substitution yields the specified diaryl/heteroaryl carbinol derivative.

questions.question_text: Amoxycillin, a polyfunctional drug has different pKa values such as 9.6, 7.4 and 2.4, at physiological pH. Groups responsible respectively are
questions.explanation: Amoxicillin contains a phenolic/carboxylic group, an amino group ($NH_3^+$), and a $\beta$-lactam/carbonyl group corresponding to these ionizable sites.

questions.question_text: A drug which has potent peripheral vasodilatory properties inhibits the voltage dependent calcium channel in vascular smooth muscle is
questions.explanation: Nifedipine is chemically dimethyl 1,4-dihydro-2,6-dimethyl-4-(2-nitrophenyl)-3,5-pyridinedicarboxylate.

questions.question_text: In the Bragg's equation $n\lambda = 2d \sin\theta$, $2\theta$ is the angle between

options.A: The direction between the incident beam and the refracted beam
options.B: The surface of the crystal and the incident fluorescent beam
options.C: The direction if the incident and that of the diffracted beam

questions.explanation: In X-ray diffraction, $2\theta$ is the scattering angle between the direction of the incident beam and the diffracted beam.

questions.question_text: The colour which the human eye perceives is not the colour corresponding to the wavelength of the light
questions.explanation: The observed color is complementary to the wavelength of light that is absorbed by the substance.

questions.question_text: During compression of moisture critical granules a hygroscopic substance used to maintain a proper moisture level is
questions.explanation: Sorbitol acts as a humectant and helps retain moisture in hygroscopic formulations.

questions.question_text: The integrated rate equation for a First order reaction is
questions.explanation: The first-order integrated rate expression is expressed in base-10 log as $\log(a/(a-x)) = kt / 2.303$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used as a local anesthetic in the formulation of parenteral products
questions.explanation: Benzyl alcohol is commonly added to multi-dose parenteral vials for its bacteriostatic and weak local anesthetic properties.

questions.question_text: In the formulation of suspensions for soft gelatin encapsulation base adsorption of the solid to be suspended is expressed as:

options.A: The number of grams of liquid base required to produce a capsulable mixture when mixed with 1 gm of solid
options.B: The number of ml of liquid base required to produce a capsulable mixture when mixed with 1 gm of Solid
options.C: The number of grams of solid base required to produce a capsulable mixture when mixed with 1 gm of solid
options.D: The number of mgs of liquid base required to produce a capsulable mixture when mixed with 10 gms of solid

questions.explanation: Base adsorption is defined as the number of grams of liquid vehicle/base required to produce a mixture of proper consistency for soft gelatin capsule filling with 1 gram of solid.

questions.question_text: The drug that binds to AT1 receptor with high affinity is
questions.explanation: Valsartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) selective for the AT1 receptor.

questions.question_text: A person taking nitroglycerine consumes alcohol. The drug interacts with alcohol and the effect seen is:
questions.explanation: Concurrent use of nitrates and alcohol can cause severe orthostatic hypotension and cardiovascular collapse due to synergistic vasodilation.

questions.question_text: The biogenetic origin of methyl substitution at $N_1$, $N_3$ and $N_7$ in caffeine molecule is:
questions.explanation: Biological methylation steps in purine alkaloid biosynthesis utilize S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) as the methyl donor.

questions.question_text: In WHO guidelines for the herbal drugs, contaminants include

options.D: Pesticidal residues, arsenic heavy metals, microbial load

questions.explanation: WHO guidelines strictly monitor pesticide residues, heavy metals like arsenic, and microbial contamination in herbal materials.

questions.question_text: The ratio of lecithin to sphingomyelin in amniotic fluid is measured

options.B: To assess fetal maturity and respiratory distress syndrome
options.C: To obtain age of the fetus
options.D: As a diagnostic marker for Tay-Sach's disease

questions.explanation: The L/S ratio is a clinical test used to assess fetal lung maturity and risk of respiratory distress syndrome.

questions.question_text: Diagnostic strips such as Diastrix/Clinistix, used commonly to monitor diabetes, work of which of the following principles:

options.A: The strips are coated with glucose oxidase, peroxidase and o-toluidine. Any glucose in the test Solution when exposed to the strips, gets oxidized leading to the release of hydrogen peroxide, the latter in turnoxidises to o-toluidine to yield a blue colour
options.B: The strips are coated with phenolphthalein analogue, which when exposed to acidic glucose solution, yield a blue colour
options.C: The strips are coated with glucose epimerase and thymol blue, which when exposed to glucose, epimerize resulting in blue colour
options.D: The strips are coated with leucine synthase and ninhydrin. Glucose, if any in the test solution gets converted into amino acids, which in turn react with ninhydrin to yield its blue colour.

questions.explanation: Clinistix/Diastrix employ an enzymatic glucose oxidase/peroxidase coupled reaction with a chromogen to detect glucose.

questions.question_text: Chemotaxis is a phenomenon that refers to

options.A: Directed movement in response to a chemical stimulus
options.C: Large in-flux of a chemical molecule within bacterial cells
options.D: Adherence of bacterial proteins to host cells

questions.explanation: Chemotaxis is the directed migratory movement of cells or organisms in response to chemical gradients.

questions.question_text: The usefulness of 5-fluorouracil as an antitumour agent can be attributed to one of the following mechanisms

options.A: It inhibits hypoxanthine guanine phophoribosyltransferase directly
options.B: It is a prodrug that gets converted to fluoro-2'-deoxy uridylic acid, which is a suicide substarte for thymidylate synthase
options.C: It gets incorporated into RNA leading to faulty transcription and translation into non-standard Aminoacids
options.D: It gets converted to tetrafluorouridylate, whichinhibitspurin nucleoside phosphorylase

questions.explanation: 5-FU is converted to FdUMP, which forms a covalent ternary complex with thymidylate synthase, acting as a mechanism-based suicide inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Gossypol, a compound which ahas received major attention as a male contraceptive: (P) Is a hydroxylatedbinaphthalene derivative found in cotton seed oil, (Q) Is an orizanol ester, found in rice bran oil, (R) Exhibits toxicity such as hypokalemic induced paralysis, (S) Acts as an androgen antagonist. Identify the correct statements.
questions.explanation: Gossypol is a binaphthalene derivative from cotton seeds and is well-known for causing hypokalemic paralysis as a toxic side effect.

questions.question_text: Acetylated benzylamine upon chlorosulfonation, amidation and hydrolysis results in a product which is used as an acetate: (P) Is Mafenide, (Q) Is N-sulfanilylacetamide, (R) For Ophthalmic infections, (S) Is 4-amino phenyl benzene sulfonamide and not a true sulfonamide. Identify the correct statements.
questions.explanation: Sulfacetamide (N-sulfanilylacetamide) is synthesized through such routes and is widely used as its sodium salt in ophthalmic anti-infective drops.

questions.question_text: Two of the following compounds give 3 signals in NMR spectroscopy. Choose the correct combination: (P) $CH_3-COOH$, (Q) $CH_3-CH_2-NH_2$, (R) $CH_3-OH$, (S) $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Cl$
questions.explanation: $CH_3-COOH$ and $CH_3-OH$ both give exactly two distinct proton environments (signals) in standard ${}^1\text{H}$ NMR, but wait, let us re-evaluate: $CH_3-COOH$ has 2 signals, $CH_3-OH$ has 2 signals. Let's check $CH_3-CH_2-NH_2$ (3 signals) and $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Cl$ (3 signals). Therefore, Q and S give 3 signals.

questions.question_text: Conductance cells for conductivity measurements can be made from two of the following metals: (P) Mercury, (Q) Sodium, (R) Platinum, (S) Stainless steel
questions.explanation: Platinum (platinized platinum) and stainless steel are standard inert/stable electrode materials used for conductance cells, whereas sodium and mercury are chemically unsuitable.

questions.question_text: In aldehydes, the $-C=O$ stretch and the $-C-H$ stretch are approximately: (P) $1725\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (Q) $1660\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (R) $2750\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (S) $3300\text{ cm}^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Aliphatic aldehyde carbonyl stretch typically occurs near $1725\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (P) and the characteristic Fermi doublet for the aldehyde C-H stretch appears around $2750\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (R).

questions.question_text: Schedule 'C' and Schedule 'N' as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act deal with the following: (P) Standards for cosmetics, (Q) Biological and special products, (R) Life period of drugs, (S) List of minimum equipments for the efficient running of a pharmacy
questions.explanation: Schedule C deals with biological and special products (Q), and Schedule N specifies the list of minimum equipment for running a pharmacy (S).

questions.question_text: Abrasive and humectant compounds used in the formulation of toothpaste are: (P) Dicalcium phosphate, (Q) Sodium lauryl sulphate, (R) Sorbitol syrup, (S) Tragacanth
questions.explanation: Dicalcium phosphate functions as an abrasive agent, and sorbitol syrup functions as a humectant in toothpaste formulations.

questions.question_text: Two of the following types of techniques are used for depot formulation: (P) Dissolution controlled, (Q) Encapsulation type, (R) Solubilization, (S) Parenteral suspensions
questions.explanation: Dissolution controlled release systems and parenteral suspensions are common classical techniques used to achieve depot drug delivery.

questions.question_text: GABA, an important transmitter in the brain: (P) Is an inhibitory transmitter, (Q) Is an excitatory transmitter, (R) Increases chloride conductance, (S) Is antagonized by Naloxone
questions.explanation: GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system (P) and exerts its action via $GABA_A$ receptors by increasing chloride ion conductance (R).

questions.question_text: Atovaquone when combined with proguanil: (P) Is highly effective and well tolerated, (Q) Is not well tolerated, (R) Antagonism is observed, (S) Resistance is reduced
questions.explanation: The combination of atovaquone and proguanil (Malarone) is highly effective, well tolerated (P), and synergistically reduces the development of parasite resistance (S).

questions.question_text: G-CSF a myeloid growth factor: (P) Exhibits action similar to that of folic acid, (Q) Has a remarkable ability to mobilize hemopoietic stem cells, (R) Is activated by t-PA, (S) Activates a phagocytic activity of mature neutrophils and prolongs their survival of circulation
questions.explanation: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells (Q) and activates phagocytic activity while prolonging mature neutrophil survival (S).

questions.question_text: Microscopical characters of cardamom are: (P) Very thin membranous arillus enveloping the seed and composed of several layers of collapsed cells, yellow in colour containing oil, (Q) Presence of anomocytic stomata on the epidermis of pericarp and mesocarp and containing lignifiedreticulate parenchyma, (R) Vittae, the secretory canals contain volatile oil and are brown in colour, (S) Inner epidermis of the pericarp are made up of polygonal tubular cells. Mesocarp includes few Brown to yellow coloured resinous cells
questions.explanation: Cardamom microscopy features a thin membranous arillus (P) and an inner epidermis of the pericarp with polygonal tubular cells along with resinous cells (S).

questions.question_text: Two of the following attributes are characteristic to a natural drug obtained from Syzygium aromaticum: (P) Qadrangular stalked portion- the hypanthium, surmounted by four divergent lobes of sepals which surround a globular head, (Q) Powdered drug shows fragments of hypantium showing the epidermis and the parenchyma containing large oil glands, singly occurring short fibres, cluster crystals of calcium oxalate, (R) Aromatic, pungent, globular berries, remains of stigma at the apex. Kernel white and hollow at the centre, consists of perisperm and endosperm, (S) Tubular epidermal cells, followed by thin walled parenchymatous hypodermis with rectangular stone cells. Pericarp and perisperm containing oil glands, abundant starch grains
questions.explanation: Syzygium aromaticum (clove) flower buds possess a quadrangular stalked hypanthium with four sepals (P) and microscopic features showing hypanthium fragments with large oil glands and calcium oxalate cluster crystals (Q).

questions.question_text: Two metabolites that could transiently accumulate as a result of inhibition of squalene synthase are: (P) Dimethylallyl pyrophosphate, (Q) Cholesterol, (R) Farnesylpyrophosphate, (S) Prednisolone
questions.explanation: Squalene synthase catalyzes the reductive dimerization of two molecules of farnesyl pyrophosphate (R) to form squalene, which is synthesized upstream via intermediates like dimethylallyl pyrophosphate (P).

questions.question_text: Two possible targets against which inhibitors can be designed for use in diabetes treatment are: (P) Carbonic anhydrase, (Q) Insulin, (R) Glycogenphosphorylase, (S) Glucose-6-phosphatase
questions.explanation: Inhibiting glycogen phosphorylase (R) and glucose-6-phosphatase (S) helps reduce hepatic glucose output, making them targets for type 2 diabetes treatment.

questions.question_text: Two important advantages of using micro-organisms for bio-transformations in drug synthesis are: (P) Having been produced from micro-organisms, they are certain to have antibacterial properties, (Q) They are abundant in nature and hence reduce the processing cost significantly, (R) They produce the specific stereoisomer only, (S) They are highly selective and therefore yield products with high purity
questions.explanation: Microbial bio-transformations offer high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity (R, S), ensuring high purity and enantiomeric excess.

questions.question_text: Aminotransferases are directly involved in the biosynthesis of: (P) Aspartate, (Q) Alanine, (R) Oleate, (S) 3-phosphoglycerate
questions.explanation: Aminotransferases catalyze the interconversion of amino acids and alpha-keto acids, directly synthesizing amino acids such as aspartate (from oxaloacetate) and alanine (from pyruvate).

questions.question_text: Match the reactions in GROUP I with their names in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) p-nitrobenzaldehyde and acetone to form 1-(4-nitrophenyl-3-oxo-butene), (Q) Isobutyl benzene is treated with acetyl chloride and anhydrous $AlCl_3$, (R) Pregnelone acetate is saponified and then treated with an aluminium alcoholate to yield progesterone, (S) Benzalacetone and 4-hydroxy coumarin in presence of pyridine. GROUP II: (1) Claisen-Schmidt condensation, (2) Michael condensation, (3) Friedel-Crafts acylation, (4) Oppenauer oxidation
questions.explanation: P corresponds to Claisen-Schmidt condensation (1), Q corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation (3), R corresponds to Oppenauer oxidation (4), and S corresponds to Michael addition/condensation (2).

questions.question_text: Match N-substitution of 4-phenylpiperidine-4-ethyl-carboxylate derivatives in GROUP I with analgesics in GROUP II. GROUP I (Substitution at N): (P) $-CH_3$, (Q) $-CH_2-CH_2-(C_6H_4)-NH_2$, (R) $-CH_2-CH_2-C-(C_6H_5)_2-CN$, (S) $-CH_2-CH_2-C_6H_5$. GROUP II (Analgesics): (1) Fentanyl, (2) Diphenoxylate, (3) Pethidine, (4) Anileridine
questions.explanation: P ($CH_3$) gives Pethidine (3); Q gives Anileridines (4); R gives Diphenoxylate (2); S gives Fentanyl derivative/related analog (1).

questions.question_text: Match drugs in GROUP I with nature and function in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Colestipolhydrochloride, (Q) Clebopride, (R) Cilazapril, (S) Mentone. GROUP II: (1) Piradizino-diazepine derivative, angiotensin Converting enzyme inhibitor, (2) Benzylpiperidine derivative, antiemetic, (3) Benzophenone derivative, topical sun screening Substance, (4) Granular copolymer of tetra ethylene and Epichlorohydrin, hypolipidemic
questions.explanation: Colestipol is a hypolipidemic polymer (P-4), Clebopride is an antiemetic benzylpiperidine derivative (Q-2), Cilazapril is an ACE inhibitor (R-1), and Menthone/Benzophenone derivative relates to sun screening/topical use (S-3).

questions.question_text: Match principles involved in GROUP I with instrument used in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Excitation of electrons, (Q) Electron impact bombardment, (R) Molecular vibration, (S) Splitting of electron's magnetic energy. GROUP II: (1) ESR spectrometer, (2) IR spectrometer, (3) Mass spectrometer, (4) UV spectrometer
questions.explanation: Electron excitation corresponds to UV (P-4), electron impact corresponds to Mass spec (Q-3), molecular vibration corresponds to IR (R-2), and electron spin splitting corresponds to ESR (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match drug in GROUP I with reagent for assay in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Albendazole, (Q) Isoniazid, (R) Sulfacetamide sodium, (S) Paracetamol. GROUP II: (1) Cerric ammonium sulphate, (2) Sodium nitrite, (3) Per chloric acid, (4) Potassium bromate
questions.explanation: Albendazole is assayed with perchloric acid (P-3), Isoniazid with potassium bromate (Q-4), Sulfacetamide with sodium nitrite diazotization (R-2), and Paracetamol with ceric ammonium sulphate (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match method adopted in GROUP I with physical state of sample used in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Gas chromatography, (Q) Infra-red, (R) HPLC, (S) X-Ray diffraction. GROUP II: (1) Solution, (2) Crystal, (3) Solid, liquid or gas, (4) Liquid or gas
questions.explanation: Gas chromatography uses liquid or gas samples (P-4), IR can use solid, liquid, or gas (Q-3), HPLC uses solution samples (R-1), and X-Ray diffraction uses crystals (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match film defects in GROUP I with explanation in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Orange peel effect, (Q) Blistering, (R) Cracking, (S) Bloom. GROUP II: (1) Inadequate spreading of the coating solution before Drying causes a bumping effect on the coating, (2) It is the result of drying coated tablets in ovens, due to too Rapid evaporation of the solvent from the core and the Effect of high temperature on the film, (3) Occurs due to processing temperature used is too high for a particular formulation, (4) Occurs if internal stress in the film exceed the tensile Strength of the film
questions.explanation: Orange peel relates to inadequate spreading/bumping (P-1), blistering relates to rapid solvent evaporation in ovens (Q-2), cracking occurs when internal stress exceeds tensile strength (R-4), and bloom relates to high temperature effects/migration (S-3).

questions.question_text: Match Group-I (term) with Group-II (example). GROUP I: (P) Hydrophilic suppository Base, (Q) Polymorphism, (R) Film former used in the Formation of nail lacquer, (S) Opaquant extender. GROUP II: (1) Nitrocellulose, (2) Titanium dioxide, (3) Cocoa butter, (4) Polyethylene glycol
questions.explanation: Hydrophilic suppository base is polyethylene glycol (P-4), polymorphism is exhibited by cocoa butter (Q-3), nail lacquer film former is nitrocellulose (R-1), and opaquant extender is titanium dioxide (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match Group-I (Drug) with Group-II (Type of action). GROUP I: (P) Toremlifene, (Q) Flutamide, (R) Ketaconazole, (S) Miglitol. GROUP II: (1) Inhibitor of adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis, (2) \alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, (3) Androgen receptor antagonist, (4) Selective estrogen receptor modulator
questions.explanation: Toremifene is a SERM (P-4), flutamide is an androgen receptor antagonist (Q-3), ketoconazole inhibits steroidogenesis (R-1/2 contextually mapped to 2/1, let's check: Miglitol is alpha-glucosidase inhibitor S-2, Ketoconazole is 1). Thus P-4, Q-3, R-1, S-2.

questions.question_text: The activities of certain object drugs are increased by certain precipitant drug choose the correct combination. GROUP I (Object drug): (P) Amines in foods, (Q) Alcohol, (R) Cefoxitin, (S) Azathioprine. GROUP II (Precipitant Drugs): (1) Allopurinol, (2) MAO inhibitor, (3) Disulfiram, (4) Probenecid
questions.explanation: MAO inhibitors increase pressor amines in foods (P-2), Disulfiram increases alcohol toxicity (Q-3), Probenecid increases antibiotic levels like cefoxitin/penicillins (R-4), Allopurinol increases azathioprine toxicity (S-1). Wait, let's match option D or corresponding pairs properly.

questions.question_text: Match GROUP I (Drug) with GROUP II (Mechanism). GROUP I: (P) Amines in foods, (Q) Alcohol, (R) Cefoxitin, (S) Azathioprine. GROUP II (Mechanism): (1) Allopurinol, (2) MAO inhibitor, (3) Disulfiram, (4) Probenecid
questions.explanation: P matches MAO inhibitor (2), Q matches Disulfiram (3), R matches Probenecid (4), and S matches Allopurinol (1).

questions.question_text: Match GROUP I (Plant Hormone Type) with GROUP II (Chemical Substance). GROUP I: (P) Auxin, (Q) Gibberellin, (R) Cytokinin, (S) Growth inhibitor. GROUP II: (1) Absicic acid, (2) NAA, (3) GA3, (4) 6-furfuryl amine
questions.explanation: Auxin corresponds to NAA (P-2), Gibberellin corresponds to GA3 (Q-3), Cytokinin corresponds to 6-furfuryl amine/kinetin (R-4), and Growth inhibitor corresponds to Abscisic acid (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match GROUP I (Crude Drugs) with GROUP II (Chemical Test). GROUP I: (P) Etoposide, (Q) Sumatra benzoin, (R) Ergot Powar, (S) Papaverine. GROUP II (Chemical Test): (1) Add a solution of potassium permanganate and warm; yield an odour of benzaldehyde, (2) To an alcoholic solution, add a solution of p-dimethylamino Benzaldehyde, (3) A solution in HCl acid when treated with k- ferriccyanide; Yield and yellow color, (4) Alcoholic solution of the drug is treated with strong copper Solution; gives a brown precipitate
questions.explanation: Benzoin gives benzaldehyde odor with KMnO4 (Q-1), Ergot alkaloids react with p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde (Van Urk's test) (R-2), Papaverine gives yellow color with ferricyanide (S-3).
